clue.text: College head wanting a good book, devoid of current jargon

parts.note: a tech is a technical college
nob is old slang for the head

indicators.note: devoid of means lacking, so a letter is taken out of the book

parts.note: the Good Book is the Bible
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A college principal without a Bible, stripped of up-to-date slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devoid of' takes I out of BIBLE, leaving BBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical-sounding language that baffles outsiders is a kind of impenetrable jargon.

clue.text: Traveller set up business supplying stuff from Virginia

indicators.note: set up, in a down clue, means raised, so the name reads bottom to top

parts.note: John Cabot was a Venetian explorer who sailed to North America
CO is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: A traveller started a business trading goods from Virginia.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia is famous for its tobacco crop, and Virginia tobacco is a known type.

clue.text: Daily story line involving male, popular actor

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a cleaning woman

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the man goes inside the story and line

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
a chap is a man
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A daily newspaper's storyline about a popular male actor.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is a British term for a cleaner, also called a char.
explanation.definitionFit: The silent-film star known for his Little Tramp character was a famous comic film actor.

clue.text: Ensure brief retraining for care worker

indicators.note: retraining means reshaping, so the remaining letters are rearranged
brief means cut short, so the last letter of ensure goes

explanation.surface: Making sure a care worker gets a quick refresher course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts the final E from ENSURE; 'retraining' rearranges ENSUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse looks after the sick, the classic person who works in care.

clue.text: Sleeping place for baby at home, protected by dog

indicators.note: protected by means surrounded by, so the dog's letters enclose the home word

parts.note: a basset is a short-legged hound
in means at home

explanation.surface: A baby's cot at home watched over by the family dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassinet is a hooded wicker cradle in which an infant sleeps.

clue.text: Very thin lad eating nothing for starters

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the lad goes round the letter

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: for starters takes the first letter of nothing

explanation.surface: A skinny boy who has eaten nothing even for a first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bony is so skinny that the bones show, which is very thin.

clue.text: Disregards hooligan crossing edge of roof

indicators.note: crossing means spanning, so the hooligan's letters go round the roof edge

parts.note: a lout is a hooligan
the eaves are the overhanging edge of a roof

explanation.surface: A hooligan climbing over the eaves ignores all warnings.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to ignore or fail to include it, so it is passed over.

clue.text: Muhammad Ali cut head, film's shown

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the final letter of the nickname is dropped

parts.note: the boxer called himself 'The Greatest'
a cape is a headland

explanation.surface: Muhammad Ali suffers a cut to the head in a film of the fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last T of THE GREATEST.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1963 Second World War prisoner-of-war movie starred Steve McQueen.

clue.text: Leader of council damned unpleasant

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of council

parts.note: ruddy is a mild British oath meaning damned

explanation.surface: The head of the council is a damned unpleasant person.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruddy is slang for dirty or of poor quality, hence nasty.

clue.text: Recalled part of serial by Orwell, in fact

indicators.note: recalled is taken as called back, so the letters are read backwards
part of says the letters sit inside the words serial by

explanation.surface: Someone remembers an episode of a serial written by George Orwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' finds RIALB in 'serial by'; 'Recalled' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell was the pen name of Eric Blair, so in fact Orwell was this man.

clue.text: Heat, with burns, affected this one?

definitions.text: Heat, with burns, affected this one?

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone suffering heat and burns: who might that be?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the person lying in the sun is the one heat and burns affect.
explanation.definitionFit: A person lying out in strong sunshine is exactly who suffers from heat and gets burnt.

clue.text: Everyone in Church Row withdrew from circulation

indicators.note: in places everyone inside the letters for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
everyone means all
a row or racket is a din

explanation.surface: Everyone in Church Row withdrew from circulation, like a street of residents going into hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Banks and governments recall old notes or coins when they cease to be legal tender.

clue.text: Asked to have some breakfast in bed?

indicators.note: in places the breakfast item inside the bed

parts.note: an egg is one item of breakfast

explanation.surface: Someone asking to be given breakfast in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg is to ask earnestly, so pleaded or requested fits asked.

clue.text: Plant, centrepiece of holy Christian festival

indicators.note: centrepiece of takes the middle letters of holy

parts.note: Easter is the Christian festival of the Resurrection

explanation.surface: A plant as the centrepiece of a holy Christian festival, like lilies on the altar.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleaster, or Russian olive, is a shrub or small tree, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Fool heading for scandal, one politician revealed

indicators.note: heading for takes the first letter of scandal

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament
let on means revealed a secret

explanation.surface: A fool of a politician heading for scandal is exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a gullible, foolish person, which is what a fool is.

clue.text: Beautiful old vase originally captured by Baroque painter

indicators.note: captured by puts the two initials inside the painter's name

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely was a Baroque portrait painter at the court of Charles II

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of each of old and vase

explanation.surface: A lovely old vase first depicted by a Baroque painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovely and beautiful are close synonyms for something pleasing to look at.

clue.text: 6 Mrs Simpson allowed to circulate urgent message

indicators.note: to circulate means to go round, so the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: Marge is Mrs Simpson of the cartoon The Simpsons
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Mrs Simpson allowed to send round an urgent message, as in the abdication crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Wallis Simpson; the Mrs Simpson needed is Marge, of the cartoon. The leading 6 is a cross-reference that plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire sent by telegraph was the traditional way to send news that could not wait.

clue.text: Plan after-school English qualification

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a degree qualification

explanation.surface: A plan for an after-school English qualification course.
explanation.definitionFit: A schema is an outline or diagrammatic scheme, which is a kind of plan.

clue.text: Joining group of workers engaged by firm

indicators.note: engaged by means held inside, so the union goes within the firm word

parts.note: firm means sure, as in certain
TU is a trade union

explanation.surface: A group of workers taken on by a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A suture is a stitch or seam that joins edges, as in surgery or bone.

clue.text: Again declared country debtridden?

definitions.meaning: said once more, repeated in words
read cryptically, a state in the red: a nation whose accounts are in deficit

explanation.surface: Someone announcing again that the country is buried in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: a country (STATE) placed in the red (RED) gives the answer, with the question mark flagging the wordplay-style reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To restate something is to say it again, so the past tense means declared a second time.

clue.text: Regularly avoided edge on trail going downhill

indicators.note: regularly avoided drops every other letter of edge, keeping the second and fourth

parts.note: a scent is a trail followed by hounds

explanation.surface: Steadily keeping away from the edge on a trail going downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link: the first piece sits on the second in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A descent is the act of going down a slope.

clue.text: Coins collected in hat for drink

indicators.note: collected in puts the coins inside the hat

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat
P stands for penny, so two coins are PP

explanation.surface: Coins passed round in a hat to buy a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: TILE is old British slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipple is an alcoholic beverage, one's favourite drink.

clue.text: Mentioned fresh flowers, in cases of illness

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the word for fresh is given by its sound

parts.note: fresh means new
roses are flowers

explanation.surface: Fresh flowers brought in for the sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuroses are mental disorders, so they are instances of illness.

clue.text: Jacket turned up and shortened? Capital

indicators.note: turned up, in a down clue, means the letters read bottom to top
shortened means its last letter is cut off

parts.note: a tabard is a sleeveless jacket or tunic

explanation.surface: A jacket taken up and shortened at the tailor's.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabat is the capital city of Morocco.

clue.text: Loyal Conservative shunning armistice

indicators.note: shunning means avoiding, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: a truce is an armistice

explanation.surface: A loyal Tory rejects a ceasefire.
explanation.definitionFit: Being true to someone means being faithful and steadfast.

clue.text: Tories excited about Republican who might join the party?

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of Tories are rearranged

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Excited Tories talking about a Republican who might join their party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks political; here it is a wild celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A roisterer is a noisy reveller, someone who would happily join a lively social gathering.

clue.text: Pair of British people

parts.note: a race is a people

explanation.surface: A pair of British people.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is two of something, as in a brace of pheasants.

clue.text: Irregular plan — queen has a hand in it

indicators.note: in it puts the queen and hand inside the plan

parts.note: an intent is an aim or plan
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen
a mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: An unpredictable plan the queen has had a hand in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intermittent starts and stops at uneven intervals, so it is not regular.
